name: One Signed Clause Can Change an Arbitrarily Remote Rooted Endpoint
statement: For every $j\ge0$ there are ordinarily peelable ample families $B_j,K_j\subseteq Q_{12+2j}$ containing zero such that $(B_j,0)$ is a rooted factor, $K_j$ peels to zero, and every proper root-preserving pc-minor of either peels to its root. Their shadows coincide and their signed minimal-nonface presentations differ only on one four-support, by antipodal omitted traces. They agree on the Hamming ball of radius $j+4$ about zero and first differ at distance $j+5$. Both have $(581\cdot3^j-3)/2$ concepts and VC dimension $3+j$; the root has degree three at $j=0$ and degree two thereafter. Hence no fixed-radius root neighborhood, even with the full shadow, determines prescribed-root peelability or rooted-factor status.
proof: At level zero, exchange the corner $1084$ for the repairing tip $604$ in the certified 289-concept factor; the exchange preserves the shadow and changes only the antipodal omitted trace on support $\{5,6,9,10\}$. Paired-square transfer recursively preserves the negative rooted factor, the positive endpoint, proper-minor positivity, and the two compatible repairs. The order recurrence is $n_{j+1}=3n_j+3$. The differences are exactly $\{1084\}\times\{01,10,11\}^j$ versus $\{604\}\times\{01,10,11\}^j$, which proves the distance claim; common punctured-cube neighbors show that every other signed clause agrees.
comments: The finite replay checks levels zero through two; the recursive proof covers every level.
